title: Formatting Output
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of formatting output and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—format specifiers—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study formatting output with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you turn raw console input into validated data and provide clear feedback for invalid values. In this lesson, focus on format specifiers and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Console input is external data. Distinguish token-reading from line-reading, validate parsed values and ranges, and make malformed or missing input produce a clear response. Apply that reasoning specifically to format specifiers and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect format specifiers with decimal precision before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Decimal precision
items.text: Operator precedence and numeric promotion determine the resulting value. Make conversions explicit when narrowing a type, and test integer boundaries and floating-point rounding instead of assuming arithmetic is exact.

items.title: Formatted reports and console tables
items.text: Treat console input as untrusted text. Validate format and range before using it, account for token-versus-line reading, and give users a clear way to correct invalid input.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.
